info.title: Whyspec shapes
info.summary: The shapes the Whyspec specification defines, as schema components.
info.description: Generated by tools/build_openapi.py from schema/*.schema.json; do not edit. This document defines no endpoints. It exists so that schema viewers can render the parsed record, the recall envelope (and the reserved command variants), the transport envelope and the intent-layer objects as navigable trees. The JSON Schema files remain the source of truth, and tools/check_schema.py keeps them consistent with the specification's prose.

parsed-record.title: Whyspec parsed record
parsed-record.description: The object a conforming parser yields from ONE record. Derived from spec/whyspec-draft.md; every property names the rule that mandates it. Where the specification is silent the property is either absent from this schema or explicitly flagged with x-gap -- nothing here is invented to fill a hole.
parsed-record.$comment: LAYERING. The specification does not cleanly separate 'the parsed record' from 'the intent node it becomes' (§2, gap G7): REC-107 speaks of both in one sentence, REC-045 places resolution_delta on the node, PROV-005/006 place provenance there, REC-112 derives currency corpus-wide. This schema carries all of them in one object and tags each with x-layer so an implementation that keeps two objects can split on that tag. NAME SPELLINGS. Several rules name a property in prose without fixing its JSON key. Where the prose fixes the spelling, x-name-source is 'rule'. Where only the conformance corpus fixes it, x-name-source is 'corpus'.

kind.description: [REC-009] The record kind, determined by which level-1 heading form matched: an `ADR-<digits><sep> <title>` H1 yields `adr`, a `Decision: <title>` H1 yields `decision`. [REC-057] MUST NOT be inferred from the record's directory. [REC-122] This is NOT the intent-kind component of node identity.

title.description: [REC-015] The matched heading text with its prefix (the `ADR-…` run and separator, or the `Decision:` literal) removed and surrounding whitespace trimmed. [REC-016] MUST be non-empty; a document whose title reduces to the empty string is not a record. [REC-017] For a `decision` record the title IS the chosen option.

rationale.description: [REC-018] The `Decision` section body, trimmed. The section is REQUIRED for a document to be a record ([REC-008]), so the key is always present. [REC-019] When several headings match, the first wins. [REC-140] An EMPTY body yields the empty string, not an absent key -- stated the opposite way from `question` ([REC-107]) because a record with no Decision section is not a record, so an absent `rationale` could never be observed.

question.description: [REC-107] The `Context` section body, yielded as `question` on the parsed record and reaching the intent node. [REC-021] The Context section carries the question the record answers. An empty or absent Context yields an ABSENT question, never an empty string -- the key is omitted entirely.

status.description: [REC-030] The status value normalized to its first run of lowercase alphabetic characters. [REC-027] Sourced from the inline `**Status:**` line or a `## Status` section; [REC-028] inline wins; [REC-029] the inline search is document-wide and first-match-wins. [REC-031] When no status can be determined the key is OMITTED ENTIRELY -- never defaulted, never an explicit null. [REC-033] No enum: only `draft`/`proposed`/`accepted`/`rejected` carry behaviour, but any other value is conventional and parses. [REC-108] `superseded` MUST NOT be a status.

deliberation.description: [REC-141] The key spelling for REC-101's Deliberation column. [REC-101] The table is the sole normative source: absent and unrecognized statuses are both `unstated`, neither is `open`, and open records are ingested and marked open.

offered.description: [REC-141] The key spelling for REC-101's Offered column. [REC-101] The table is the sole normative source and distinguishes `draft` from `proposed` through this field.

disposition.description: [REC-141] The key spelling for REC-101's Disposition column, already fixed at the envelope by [ENV-022]. [REC-101] The table is the sole normative source for the value; a null is carried where the table gives no disposition. [REC-104] A `declined` record yields foreclosure intent: retained and queryable, never counted as trusted evidence, never presented as team practice. [PROV-019] A result containing intent MUST expose this. [PROV-017] Independent of provenance.

alternatives.description: [REC-134] Each item is an OBJECT carrying `option` and, where recorded, `disposition` and `rationale`; this supersedes REC-018's earlier 'ordered list of strings'. [ENV-016] still governs the ENVELOPE field of the same name, which projects `option` text only. [REC-022] Parsed as a FLAT list, every marker at top level. [REC-023] Each item's whitespace collapsed, trimmed, every `**` sequence removed. [REC-024] Yielded in document order. [REC-025] A prose (list-free) section yields an EMPTY list, not an error and not the prose. Absent section yields an empty list too.

recommendation.description: [REC-018] The `Recommendation` section body, trimmed. Optional section; the key is absent when no such section exists.

resolution_delta.description: [REC-045] Present on the intent node when a `Recommendation` body differs from the trimmed title. [REC-046] OMITTED ENTIRELY from the node when the recommendation is absent, empty, or equal to the title. Note the deliberate divergence at the envelope: [ENV-037] requires the CAPTURE envelope to carry it present-with-explicit-null instead.

assumptions.description: [REC-018] A list of structured claims yielded from the `Assumptions` section. [REC-034] Each list item (parsed per REC-022--REC-025) yields one assumption. An absent section yields an empty list. [REC-032] A rejected record's assumptions MUST NOT become ground-truth intent either.

supersedes.description: [REC-040] Every match of `\bsupersedes?\s+(ADR-\d+)` collected case-insensitively over the whole document. [REC-041] The passive form 'superseded by ADR-N' MUST NOT be collected. [REC-042] Uppercased, de-duplicated, yielded in first-seen order. Empty list when the document declares none.

identifier.description: [REC-075] The citational record identifier from the inline `**Id:** <value>` field. [REC-076] Read verbatim; MUST NOT be regenerated or derived from mutable record content and remains stable across edits. [REC-078] Unique within a corpus; two records sharing one leaves neither as the referent. Absent when no `Id` line was written.

attribution.description: [REC-079] A list yielded from the `## Attribution` section, one entry per list item, each of the form `<role> <kind>:<id> [on <date>]`. [REC-081] Any number of entries, including several sharing a role; an ABSENT section means unrecorded and MUST NOT be defaulted or inferred, so the key is omitted rather than empty. [REC-115] Roles are distinct and MUST NOT be collapsed by actor.

self_ratification.description: [REC-141] The key spelling REC-118's marking is carried under, on the record. [REC-118] True when a ratifying actor also carries the role `drafted` or `decided` on this record. MUST be marked, MUST NOT promote provenance, and [REC-120] MUST NOT cause the attribution to be discarded. [REC-128] 'The same actor' is the (kind, id) PAIR compared as written.

governs.description: [REC-082] Artifact references from the `## Governs` section, one per list item, each taken VERBATIM: list markers are stripped per REC-022 and empty items dropped per REC-025, but REC-023's emphasis-stripping and whitespace normalization MUST NOT be applied (they would destroy `src/**/*.py`). [REC-083] Exactly one reference kind is defined: a repository-relative path glob. [REC-084] An ABSENT section means 'scope not declared' and MUST NOT be read as 'governs nothing' -- the key is OMITTED, never an empty array. [PROV-013] A declared scope binding takes the declaring record's provenance.

validity.description: [REC-164] The `## Validity` section body, trimmed: the one condition under which the decision stops applying, carried as prose and taken VERBATIM in the sense of REC-082 -- REC-023's emphasis-stripping and whitespace normalization MUST NOT be applied, because a code span is how the condition names what it depends on. [REC-165] An ABSENT section means 'no condition declared' and MUST NOT be read as 'the decision never stops applying' -- the key is OMITTED, never an empty string. [REC-166] A body that does not begin `This stops applying when` is still yielded here and is not a declared condition. [REC-170] Distinct from an assumption's free-text REC-037 `expiry`; neither is derived from the other.

validity_referents.description: [REC-167] The validity referents of a declared condition, in document order: the contents of each code span in the body, yielded VERBATIM as REC-082 yields a declared scope item. Text outside a code span declares no referent. A referent is resolved as declared scope is -- REC-153's normalization, REC-152's three path forms, REC-151's `<path>#<symbol>` reference -- and a reader MUST NOT search the tree for a bare symbol name. The key is OMITTED where the section is absent or its body is not a declared condition (REC-166); an empty array is a declared condition naming none, which REC-168 records and does not test. [REC-169] A referent resolving to zero artifacts is reported as a named state, as REC-086 requires of declared scope.

relations.description: [REC-087] Declared relations from the `## Relations` section, one per list item, in the form `<relation> <identifier>`. [REC-090] A relation whose target cannot be resolved is dropped silently; [REC-091] an AMBIGUOUS target is also dropped and MUST NOT be resolved by any tiebreak. [PROV-013] Every relation carries provenance: a declared relation takes the declaring record's tier and an inferred relation is `reconstructed`.

evidence.description: [REC-093] Entries from the `## Evidence` section, one per list item, in the form `<method>: <qualifier>` with the qualifier optional. [REC-096] A record with no `## Evidence` section records NOTHING about method: the key is omitted, it MUST NOT be read as 'no evidence existed', and it MUST NOT be flagged. [REC-095] A citation of deliberation MUST be a reference; deliberation content MUST NOT be embedded and this specification defines no field for it.

provenance.description: [PROV-001] One of exactly four values; the set is closed. [PROV-005] An ADR record with no `## Attribution` yields `authored`; [PROV-006] a decision record with no `## Attribution` yields `captured`. [PROV-021] Where attribution IS present the tier is determined by ratification and NOT by record kind, and a record with no corroborated ratification is `captured` whatever its heading form. [REC-119] A ratification alone MUST NOT promote to `authored`. [PROV-003] Absent or unrecognized provenance ranks as `reconstructed`. [PROV-007] An assumption node SHOULD inherit its record's tier.

confidence_score.description: [PROV-008] Intent ingested from a record MUST carry a numeric confidence of 1.0 -- the record IS the evidence. [PROV-009] MUST NOT be conflated with provenance: filtering and merging use this number only, trust decisions use provenance only.

id.description: [REC-123] The node identity: `intent_` followed by the first 12 characters of the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-1 digest of the joined identity string, UTF-8 encoded. [REC-071] The joined string is `<canonical source path> :: <source location> :: <intent kind> :: <normalized label>`; [REC-121] joined by exactly `::` with NO surrounding whitespace. [REC-124] Only the label is normalized ([REC-072]); the source location is hashed as it appears. This is content-derived and changes when the content changes -- it is not the citational `identifier` of REC-075.

intent_kind.description: [REC-122] The kind of the NODE, exactly `decision` or `assumption`. An ADR-headed record still produces a decision node, and `adr` MUST NOT appear in an identity. This is the third identity component of REC-071.

source_file.description: [REC-073] The canonical source path: the repository-relative path in POSIX separator form. An absolute path MUST be resolved (collapsing symlink aliases) and made relative to the repository root before hashing; a relative path is left byte-identical apart from separator normalization. [REC-074] A path outside any repository falls back to a POSIX-normalized absolute spelling, and canonicalization MUST NOT raise. First identity component of REC-071.

source_location.description: [REC-071] The second identity component. [REC-124] Hashed AS IT APPEARS, without normalization. §4.12: for a decision node the source location and the label are both the record title. [REC-127] For an ASSUMPTION node both are the claim as REC-038 yields it -- after the review-date and expiry strippings, whitespace-collapsed, trimmed of spaces and periods -- taken verbatim. `review_by` and `expiry` are NOT identity inputs, so editing a review date MUST NOT fork the node.

label.description: [REC-071] The fourth identity component, hashed after normalization. [REC-072] The normalized label is the label lowercased, every run of characters outside `[a-z0-9]` replaced by `_`, and leading/trailing `_` stripped. [REC-124] The label is the ONLY component that is normalized. [REC-127] For an assumption node the label before normalization is the claim as REC-038 yields it, same as `source_location`.

currency.description: [REC-111] Whether the decision is still live. MUST be derived from the relation graph and MUST NOT be authored on the record. [REC-112] `historical` when at least one other record declares a `supersedes` relation naming it, `current` otherwise; defined ONLY for records whose disposition is `adopted`, so the key is omitted for an open or declined record. [REC-113] Supersession applies transitively. [REC-114] A record in a supersession CYCLE is `indeterminate`, and MUST NOT be resolved by any tiebreak.

format_version.description: [VER-011] The format version the record declares via `**Whyspec:** MAJOR.MINOR`; absent when the record states none or the marker is malformed. A parser never rejects a record for an unknown version.

date.description: [REC-159] The record's date from the inline `**Date:** <value>` field: a full ISO-8601 calendar date, or the leading one when an annotation follows; absent when the line is missing or malformed. [REC-047] Emitted adjacent to Status.

parsed-record.alternative.title: Structured alternative
parsed-record.alternative.description: [REC-097] An alternative item MAY carry a disposition and a rejection rationale, in the form `<option> — <disposition>: <rationale>`.

option.description: [REC-097] The option text. [REC-133] The separator is an em dash, en dash or hyphen-minus with whitespace on EACH side -- which is what keeps `blue-green deploy` from splitting. [REC-099] An alternative carrying no disposition yields the WHOLE item as its option text, separator included; a separator with no recognized disposition token after it MUST NOT be split.

disposition.description: [REC-098] One of exactly `rejected`, `deferred`, `partially-adopted`, `not-evaluated`. The set is closed; adding one requires a version marker (§7). [REC-133] The token is matched CASE-INSENSITIVELY and yielded LOWERCASED; an item whose token is outside the set carries no disposition at all. [REC-099] ABSENT (key omitted) when the item carries none -- absence means not recorded, never that no disposition existed. [REC-100] `deferred` MUST NOT be treated as equivalent to `rejected`.

rationale.description: [REC-097] The rejection rationale following the disposition. [REC-099] ABSENT (key omitted) when the item carries no disposition.

parsed-record.assumption.title: Assumption
parsed-record.assumption.description: [REC-034] One assumption per list item in the `Assumptions` section, with a `claim` plus two optional fields.

claim.description: [REC-034] The claim. [REC-038] After the review-date and expiry strippings, normalized by collapsing whitespace and trimming spaces AND periods from both ends.

review_by.description: [REC-035] Captured from `\(?\s*review[ -]by:?\s*(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\s*\)?` case-insensitively and REMOVED from the claim text. [REC-036] A full ISO-8601 calendar date, `YYYY-MM-DD`; this is the machine-checkable field. [REC-039] OMITTED ENTIRELY when not present, never serialized as null.

expiry.description: [REC-037] Captured from `\(\s*expires?:?\s*([^)]+?)\s*\)` case-insensitively and REMOVED from the claim text. FREE TEXT and not machine-checkable: it records a condition, not a date. [REC-039] OMITTED ENTIRELY when not present, never serialized as null.

parsed-record.attribution.title: Attribution
parsed-record.attribution.description: [REC-079] One attribution per list item, in the form `<role> <kind>:<id> [on <date>]`. Attribution is a relation, not a field.

role.description: [REC-080] One of exactly `drafted`, `decided`, `ratified`. The set is closed; adding to it requires a version marker (§7). [REC-115] `drafted` names who composed the record, `decided` who chose among the alternatives, `ratified` who accepted it through a review process -- these MUST NOT be conflated.

kind.description: [REC-080] One of exactly `human` or `agent`. The set is closed; adding to it requires a version marker (§7).

id.description: [REC-079] The actor identifier from the `<kind>:<id>` term. [REC-128] An ACTOR is the ordered pair (kind, id); two actors are the same actor iff BOTH components are equal, compared as written. REC-118's self-ratification check MUST compare the pair, never this field alone -- `human:alex` and `agent:alex` are different actors.

date.description: [REC-117] An attribution MAY carry a date. Where present it MUST be a full ISO-8601 calendar date. Omitted when the item carries none. [REC-129] A date that is present but MALFORMED is yielded ABSENT: the bad value MUST NOT be yielded, widened or repaired, and the attribution itself MUST NOT be dropped -- who did what does not depend on when being typed correctly.

provenance.description: [REC-117] Each attribution MUST carry its own provenance (§5.5). [PROV-013] An edge MUST carry its own provenance and MUST NOT inherit it from either node it connects. [PROV-001] The closed four-value set.

corroborated.description: [REC-141] The key spelling REC-119's marking is carried under, on the attribution. [REC-119] For a `ratified` role: whether corroboration external to the record was found. An implementation unable to corroborate MUST mark the ratification uncorroborated, MUST NOT promote, and MUST leave the record at `captured`. [REC-120] An uncorroborated ratification MUST NOT be discarded.

parsed-record.relation.title: Declared relation
parsed-record.relation.description: [REC-087] One relation per list item, in the form `<relation> <identifier>`.

relation.description: [REC-088] One of exactly `supersedes`, `refines`, `constrains`, `motivated_by`, `trade_off_against`, `contradicts`. The set is closed; adding a relation requires a version marker (§7).

target.description: [REC-089] A record identifier ([REC-075]) or an ADR number.

provenance.description: [PROV-013] Every relation object MUST carry provenance. A declared relation takes the provenance of its declaring record; an inferred relation MUST be `reconstructed` and MUST NOT be presented as declared.

parsed-record.evidence.title: Evidence entry
parsed-record.evidence.description: [REC-093] One entry per list item, in the form `<method>: <qualifier>`, where the qualifier is optional.

method.description: [REC-094] One of exactly `grep`, `diff`, `executed`, `read`, `traced`. The set is closed; an unrecognized method is a validation error AT CAPTURE TIME, not a silently unflagged value. [REC-130] On the READ path the entry is DROPPED and the value MUST NOT be yielded as a method; other entries parse unchanged and the record still parses, because an evidence defect is not a record-gate defect ([REC-008]).

qualifier.description: [REC-093] The optional qualifier after the method. Omitted when the entry carries none.

envelope.title: Whyspec result envelope
envelope.description: [ENV-001] A query result MUST be a single JSON object -- not an array, not a stream of objects, not a bare value. [ENV-005] Modelled as a TAGGED UNION discriminated by `command` over a universal core of {command, status}, never as one struct with many optional fields. Key sets are taken from the §6.1 table and the ENV-0nn enumerations; every property names the rule that mandates it.
envelope.$comment: The core command variants are closed tagged-union members: each known command accepts only its own declared top-level keys. `command` itself has no enum because [VER-004] makes adding a command a vocabulary extension and [ENV-008] requires consumers to fail safely on an unknown tag. Transport metadata is outside this core schema and is specified by the separate transport profile. Nested result entries remain open where their governing rule does not state an exact key set.

command.description: [ENV-002] Every envelope MUST carry `command`: a stable lowercase string naming the operation that produced it. [ENV-004] With `status`, one of the only two universal keys. [ENV-005] The union discriminator.

status.description: [ENV-003] Every envelope MUST carry `status`: a lowercase snake_case token classifying the outcome. [ENV-007] Status tokens are PER-COMMAND, not global. [ENV-009] MUST NOT be overloaded to carry data. [ENV-010] An honest negative is a complete answer, not an error.

envelope.error_envelope.title: Error variant (any command)
envelope.error_envelope.description: [ENV-011] An envelope reporting a failure MUST carry `command`, `status` and a human-readable `message`, MUST NOT require variant-specific keys, and consumers cannot assume those keys from `command` alone. [ENV-007] The two input-failure tokens available to any command.

status.description: [ENV-007] `no_intent_layer` or `error` -- the tokens the table lists for 'any (input failure)'.

envelope.why_ok.title: why
envelope.why_ok.description: [ENV-013] The `why` envelope MUST carry `query` (the question as asked), `count` (number of results returned), `cutoff` (the strong-match score threshold in effect), `score_stats` and `results`.

status.description: [ENV-007] `why` emits `ok`, `weak_match`, `topically_weak`, `no_strong_match`. [ENV-019] `topically_weak` means the top result cleared the cutoff but its match evidence does not support treating it as an answer -- an abstention ABOVE the cutoff, which a consumer MUST NOT treat as equivalent to `ok`. [ENV-020] `weak_match` means the top result scored UNDER the cutoff but stands clearly apart from the runner-up.

count.description: [ENV-013] Number of results returned. §6.1: not universal -- `count` appears on `why` and `list-intent` and nowhere else.

cutoff.description: [ENV-013] The strong-match score threshold in effect. §1.4: the threshold's VALUE and the scoring function are out of scope.

score_stats.description: [ENV-014] An object with `top`, `runner_up` and `median`, computed over the WHOLE scored field, not only the returned rows.

top.description: [ENV-014] Highest score over the whole scored field.

runner_up.description: [ENV-014] Second score over the whole scored field.

median.description: [ENV-014] Median score over the whole scored field.

note.description: §6.1: `why` carries an eighth key, `note`, WHEN AND ONLY WHEN `status` is `topically_weak`. [ENV-004] A variant's key set is keyed on the status it carries, so an implementation MUST NOT assert an exact key count for a variant without naming the status it holds for.

envelope.why_result.title: why result entry
envelope.why_result.description: [ENV-015] Each entry in `results` MUST carry `disposition`, `score`, `id`, `label`, `intent_kind`, `claim`, `rationale`, `alternatives`, `source_file`, `source_location`, `provenance`, `matched_terms`, `distinctive_matches`, `matched_coverage`. [PROV-019] `disposition` is there because a result containing intent MUST expose it.

score.description: [ENV-015] This row's score. §1.4: how it is computed is out of scope.

id.description: [ENV-015] The node identity. [REC-123] `intent_` plus 12 lowercase hex characters of a SHA-1 digest.

label.description: [ENV-015] The node label. [REC-071] The fourth identity component, before normalization.

intent_kind.description: [ENV-015] The kind of the node. [ENV-047] This ENVELOPE field is NOT constrained to REC-122's pair, so no enum is stated here. [REC-122] closes the intent-kind IDENTITY COMPONENT at exactly `decision` or `assumption` for a node derived from a record, and forbids `adr`; an implementation MUST NOT hash any other value as that component, and MUST NOT reject an envelope carrying another value here. [ENV-033] presupposes a `constraint` kind at envelope level, and §1.4 puts intent derived from non-record sources out of scope.

rationale.description: [ENV-015] [REC-018] The `Decision` section body of the source record.

alternatives.description: [ENV-016] MUST be a list of strings. An implementation reading a legacy scalar MUST coerce it to a single-element list, and MUST NOT iterate a bare string character by character.
alternatives.x-conflict: ENV-016's 'list of strings' cannot carry the per-item disposition and rationale that REC-097--REC-099 require. See REC-133.

source_file.description: [ENV-015] [REC-073] The canonical, repository-relative POSIX source path.

provenance.description: [ENV-015] [PROV-001] One of exactly four values. [PROV-004] The primary sort key when results are ordered by trust.

matched_terms.description: [ENV-017] Which of the question's terms matched this result at all. An implementation MUST NOT redefine this.

distinctive_matches.description: [ENV-017] The SUBSET of `matched_terms` whose matched corpus token is corpus-distinctive rather than shared by nearly every record. A term every record contains carries no topical evidence.

matched_coverage.description: [ENV-017] The fraction of the question's CONTENT terms that matched. [ENV-018] MUST be in [0, 1] inclusive.

disposition.description: The disposition of the record this result derives from — adopted or declined. Required by [PROV-019] so a consumer can partition commitments from foreclosures without inspecting record text.

filter.description: [ENV-021] MUST echo the filter that was applied, with an EXPLICIT NULL for each unset criterion -- a consumer must be able to see what was not filtered. [ENV-038] Present-with-null therefore means 'applicable, and not set', which an omitted key could not say.

intent_kind.description: [ENV-022] The kind of the node. [ENV-047] This envelope field is NOT constrained to REC-122's pair, so no enum is stated here; the rule governs the field wherever it appears, not only on a `why` result. [REC-122] closes the intent-kind IDENTITY COMPONENT for a node derived from a record. [ENV-033] presupposes a `constraint` kind and §1.4 puts non-record intent out of scope.

confidence_score.description: [ENV-022] [PROV-008] Intent ingested from a record MUST carry a numeric confidence of 1.0. [PROV-009] Orthogonal to provenance: filtering and merging use this number only.

disposition.description: [ENV-022] [PROV-019] A result containing intent MUST expose disposition, so a consumer can partition commitments from foreclosures without inspecting record text. [REC-101] `adopted` or `declined`; explicit null while deliberation is open or unstated. [PROV-017] Independent of provenance -- being declined MUST NOT lower a tier, and a strong tier MUST NOT make a foreclosure read as a commitment.

envelope.explain_ok.title: explain (ok)
envelope.explain_ok.description: [ENV-023] The `ok` variant MUST carry `query`, `resolved`, `intent`, `explains` and `relations`. [ENV-006] `explain`'s three disjoint shapes are keyed by `status`, which a consumer MUST apply before reading any variant-specific key.

resolved.description: [ENV-023] MUST report how the argument was matched (`matched_by`) and, for a non-exact match, a `score`.

relations.description: [ENV-023] The intent's relations. [PROV-013] Each edge carries its own provenance and MUST NOT inherit it from either node.

envelope.explain_ambiguous.title: explain (ambiguous)
envelope.explain_ambiguous.description: [ENV-024] The `ambiguous` variant MUST carry `candidates` and `message` and MUST NOT carry `resolved`. Ambiguity is not a partial answer; an implementation MUST NOT silently pick a candidate.

candidates.description: [ENV-024] The candidates the argument resolved to.

envelope.explain_not_found.title: explain (not_found)
envelope.explain_not_found.description: [ENV-004] §6.1 table: the `explain` (not_found) row carries `command`, `status`, `query`, `message`. [ENV-010] An honest negative is a complete answer, not an error.

envelope.changed_ok.title: changed
envelope.changed_ok.description: [ENV-025] The `changed` envelope MUST carry `base` (the reference diffed against, or null when files were supplied explicitly), `changed_files`, `files_with_intent` and `results`.

status.description: [ENV-007] `changed` emits `ok`, `no_intent_governing_changes`. [ENV-010] The negative is a complete answer.

base.description: [ENV-025] The reference diffed against, or an explicit NULL when files were supplied explicitly. [ENV-038] Present-with-null, not omitted.

file.description: [ENV-025] The file this result is about.

ambiguous.description: [ENV-026] MUST be true when the file was matched by BASENAME and that basename resolves to more than one path. A basename match that could mean several files MUST be reported as such rather than silently resolved.

governed_by.description: [ENV-025] The intent governing this file. [PROV-015] A binding between intent and an artifact is `reconstructed` unless it was DECLARED (§4.15).

superseded.description: [ENV-027] Intent superseded since. [REC-111] Currency is derived from the relation graph, never authored.

envelope.coverage_summary.title: coverage (corpus-wide summary)
envelope.coverage_summary.description: [ENV-044] The summary variant MUST carry exactly twelve coverage-specific keys alongside `command` and `status`; the `required` list below is that rule and nothing else. Two of the twelve are the trusted-evidence block (`golden`) and the debt block (`intent_debt`). [ENV-006] The discriminator against the explain variant is the ABSENCE of the `explain` key; the two shapes share no keys beyond `command` and `status`.

code_files.description: [ENV-044] One of the twelve coverage-specific keys. No rule states its type.

code_symbols.description: [ENV-044] One of the twelve coverage-specific keys. No rule states its type.

files_with_intent.description: [ENV-044] One of the twelve coverage-specific keys. No rule states its type.

symbols_with_intent.description: [ENV-044] One of the twelve coverage-specific keys. No rule states its type.

authored_anchored_files.description: [ENV-044] One of the twelve coverage-specific keys. No rule states its type.

authored_anchored_symbols.description: [ENV-044] One of the twelve coverage-specific keys. No rule states its type.

file_coverage_pct.description: [ENV-044] One of the twelve coverage-specific keys. No rule states its type or its scale; the corpus writes a percentage, not a fraction.

symbol_coverage_pct.description: [ENV-044] One of the twelve coverage-specific keys. No rule states its type or its scale; the corpus writes a percentage, not a fraction.

dark_files.description: [ENV-049] An array of repository-relative paths — the files carrying no intent. MUST NOT be a count: the count lives in `intent_debt.dark_files` ([ENV-045]), so an array here makes the pair complementary rather than duplicating one number and losing the paths.

intent_by_kind.description: [ENV-044] One of the twelve coverage-specific keys. [ENV-047] Its keys are node kinds and are NOT constrained to REC-122's pair; the corpus carries `constraint`, `mechanism` and `tradeoff` beside `decision` and `assumption`.

golden.description: [ENV-050] The trusted-evidence block. Five components, all required.

by_provenance.description: [ENV-050] Every tier mapped to its count; required alongside the percentage by [PROV-012].

golden_fraction_pct.description: [ENV-050] Integer percentage. MUST NOT be reported without by_provenance ([PROV-012]).

intent_debt.description: [ENV-045] The debt block carries EXACTLY four components, each a non-negative integer or an explicit null, and none of them MAY be omitted -- that last clause is what makes ENV-029 enforceable, since an implementation could otherwise satisfy it by dropping the key. [ENV-029] A component the implementation CANNOT COMPUTE MUST be reported as an explicit null, never as 0 -- a zero claims 'we measured and found none', a null honestly says 'not measured'. [ENV-039] Where the spec names a present-with-null field the key MUST be present.

dark_files.description: [ENV-045] A non-negative integer, or an explicit null where it cannot be computed ([ENV-029]). Note this is a COUNT; the top-level `dark_files` key is a separate field whose type is contested.

orphaned_intent.description: [ENV-045] A non-negative integer, or an explicit null where it cannot be computed ([ENV-029]).

stale_decisions.description: [ENV-045] A non-negative integer, or an explicit null where it cannot be computed ([ENV-029]).

unresolved_disputes.description: [ENV-045] A non-negative integer, or an explicit null where it cannot be computed ([ENV-029]).

envelope.coverage_explain.title: coverage (per-file explain form)
envelope.coverage_explain.description: [ENV-004] §6.1 table: carries `command`, `status`, `explain`, `trace_present`, `referencing_intent`, `counts`. [ENV-006] The discriminator is the PRESENCE of the `explain` key; the two coverage shapes share no keys beyond `command` and `status`, and a consumer MUST apply the discriminator before reading any variant key.

status.description: [ENV-007] The explain form emits `ok`, `no_references`. [ENV-010] `no_references` is a complete answer, not an error.

envelope.check_ok.title: check
envelope.check_ok.description: [ENV-030] The `check` envelope MUST carry `rules` (count of rules evaluated), `files_checked` and `violations`.

rules.description: [ENV-030] Count of rules evaluated. [ENV-032] A rule of a type the checker does not implement MUST be SKIPPED -- never counted as a pass and never as a failure.

envelope.violation.title: check violation
envelope.violation.description: [ENV-048] Each violation MUST carry `rule`, `file`, `message`, and the `decision_id` of the decision it cites. A rule whose failure cannot name the decision that motivated it is not a conformance check; it is a lint.

rule.description: [ENV-048] The identifier of the rule that was evaluated.

file.description: [ENV-048] The file the violation was found in.

message.description: [ENV-048] The human-readable description of the violation.

decision_id.description: [ENV-048] The identifier of the decision this violation cites -- a rule whose failure cannot name the decision that motivated it is a lint, not a conformance check.

envelope.intent_diff_ok.title: intent-diff
envelope.intent_diff_ok.description: [ENV-004] §6.1 table: carries `command`, `status`, `base`, `summary`, `introduces`, `supersedes`, `governed`, `constraint_review`. [ENV-033] MUST distinguish 'governed by a decision' from 'governed by a constraint': deterministic inspection cannot tell conformance from violation, so a constraint touch MUST NOT be reported as a proven violation.

supersedes.description: [ENV-004] §6.1 table. [REC-111] Currency is derived from the relation graph.

governed.description: [ENV-004] §6.1 table. [ENV-033] Governed BY A DECISION, kept distinct from a constraint touch.

constraint_review.description: [ENV-004] §6.1 table. [ENV-033] Governed BY A CONSTRAINT -- a touch, never a proven violation.

envelope.review_context_ok.title: review-context
envelope.review_context_ok.description: [ENV-004] §6.1 table: carries `command`, `status`, `base`, `changed_files`, `governing`, `unresolved_constraints`, `guidance`. [ENV-033] MUST distinguish 'governed by a decision' from 'governed by a constraint'.

status.description: [ENV-007] `review-context` emits `ok`, `no_intent_governing_changes`. [ENV-010] The negative is a complete answer.

unresolved_constraints.description: [ENV-004] §6.1 table. [ENV-033] Constraint touches, never proven violations.

envelope.capture_ok.title: capture
envelope.capture_ok.description: [ENV-034] The `capture` envelope MUST carry `record` (the path as given, from which node identity derives), `record_abs` (the resolved absolute destination), `node_id`, `title`, `provenance`, `resolution_delta` and `merged`.

record.description: [ENV-034] The path AS GIVEN, which is required alongside the absolute destination because node identity derives from this spelling. [REC-073] Identity hashes the canonical spelling of this path.

record_abs.description: [ENV-034] The resolved absolute destination, required alongside the relative spelling so a success envelope cannot hide a write into an unrelated working tree.

node_id.description: [ENV-034] [REC-123] The node identity: `intent_` plus 12 lowercase hex characters of a SHA-1 digest.

title.description: [ENV-034] [REC-017] The chosen option, which for a decision record IS the title.

resolution_delta.description: [ENV-034] [ENV-037] MUST be present with an EXPLICIT NULL when there was no delta -- a deliberate exception to [ENV-038], because the consumer of this field asks a yes/no question that a missing key cannot answer. [REC-045] The object is `{recommended, chosen}`.

merged.description: [ENV-034] [ENV-036] MUST report whether the derived view was updated, INDEPENDENTLY of `status`. Writing the record and failing to update a derived index is an honest partial success: it MUST NOT be reported as a failure and MUST NOT be reported as an unqualified success.

transport-envelope.title: Whyspec result-envelope transport profile
transport-envelope.description: [ENV-040] A transport credential is outside the core envelope and is validated as a separate profile. Validate the object with this schema and validate the projection without `graph_identity` against the core envelope schema.

graph_identity.description: [ENV-040] `graph_identity` is a transport credential block. [ENV-041] It is always present on this profile and is explicit null when no identity resolved.

intent-layer.title: Whyspec intent-layer profile objects
intent-layer.description: [INT-001] The three optional intent-layer objects. Validate a document against the $def named for its kind.

tree_sha.description: [INT-002] The commit the scope was resolved against, or null outside version control.

scope.description: [INT-002] Scope items in the artifact-reference grammar of §4.15 (REC-083); non-empty.

goal.description: [INT-002] [INT-004] The goal, or null until the writer supplies it on a harness-derived record.

approach.description: [INT-002] [INT-004] The approach, or null until supplied.

matched.description: [INT-004] Each scope item mapped to the count of artifacts it resolved to at declaration.

session.description: [INT-002] The harness's session identifier, or null.

origin.description: [INT-003] Who produced the scope: the writer, or the harness from what the session read.

scope_capped.description: [INT-003] Present on every harness-derived record as a boolean, true when the cap was applied; absent on an agent-declared record.

tree_sha.description: [INT-006] The commit the session's work stands at.

intention.description: [INT-006] The intention record answered, or null where none was recorded.

conformed.description: [INT-006] [INT-008] Records the work followed, each with the content hash of the version followed.

superseded.description: [INT-006] [INT-007] [INT-008] Records the work departed from; every entry enters as proposed.

none.description: [INT-006] Scope items for edited files no record governs.

session.description: [INT-006] The harness's session identifier, or null.
[INT-010] The harness's session identifier, or null.

tool_use_id.description: [INT-010] The harness's identifier for the accompanying tool call, or null.

records.description: [INT-010] [INT-011] Record paths delivered; empty unless push_outcome is pushed.

push_outcome.description: [INT-011] pushed, none_governs, or resolution_failed — honest silence made mechanical.

reason.description: [INT-010] Present when and only when push_outcome is resolution_failed.

tree_sha.description: [INT-010] The commit the resolution ran against.

coupling.description: [INT-012] edit, intention, or the reserved spawn.
